To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oncogenic transformation of fibroblastic cell lines by the BCR-ABl oncoprotein requires expression of the IL3 receptor.

oncogenic transformation of the fibroblastic NIH 3T 3 cells by BCR-ABl requires expression of the IL3 receptor, and that this receptor activates both the Jak2/PI- 3 kinase pathway and the Stat5 signaling pathway.
oncogenic transformation of fibroblasts by the Bcr/Abl oncoprotein is dependent on the IL-3/IL-3Rα/β chain receptor and that the Jak2/Stat5 pathway is critical for this oncogenic transformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of BCR-ABl-induced oncogenesis.
the mechanisms of oncogenesis induced by BCR-ABl, a protein that is the cause of chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in 90% of the cases.
the molecular basis of oncogenic transformation by the BCR-ABl oncogene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL-3R/JAK2 pathway is required for BCR-ABL-mediated transformation of NIH 13T3 fibroblast cells.

the Jak2/Stat5 signaling pathway is required for Bcr-Abl-induced transformation of NIH 31T3 cells, and that this pathway is normally utilized by the IL-3/granulocytic macrophage colony-stimulate factor receptors.
the IL-3/Jak2/STAT5 pathway is required for oncogenic transformation by Bcr-Abla, and that the IL-2/Jak2/PI3 kinase pathway is not required for oncogenicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oncogenic transformation of fibroblasts by BCR- ABL requires both the IL-3R and Jak2, but not the Stat5 pathway.

the IL-3/IL-3R pathway is essential for BCR-ABL-mediated transformation in fibroblasts, and that the Jak2 kinase and the Stat pathway are critical for the transformation of fibroblasts by BCR-ABl, but not the Jak1/Stat1 pathway, which is required for transformation of hematopoetic cells by BCR- ABL.
the Jak2/Stat5 pathway is essential for oncogenic transformation by Bcr-Ahl, and that the IL-3/IL-3R pathway provides the necessary signaling for Jak2 to be activated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL-3/granulocytic-macrophage receptor/Jak2 signaling pathway is required for BCR-ABL-mediated transformation of NIH 13 cells.
the Jak2/Stat5 pathway is required for oncogenic transformation and that the Jak2 inhibitor AG490 is a potent inhibitor of Bcr-Abl oncogenic transformation.
the Jak2/Stat5 pathway plays a critical role in the oncogenic transformation of fibroblasts by BCR-ABL.
